The app edits `buf` in place and calls `lv_obj_invalidate` without calling `lv_label_set_text(obj, NULL)`, a pattern the old code handled because it measured on every draw. `size.x` is now the old string's width, so the second circular copy is drawn at the wrong offset (overlapping, or with a gap). If the new string no longer overflows, the copy may be drawn when it shouldn't be, or skipped when it should be."

    "failure_scenario": "A static or in-place-modified text in SCROLL mode with CENTER alignment grows past the label width without a refresh. The cached `size.x` is still smaller than the width, so the alignment stays CENTER while the text overflows. You get the misalignment the comment says this block exists to prevent."

    "failure_scenario": "Table cells with `LV_TABLE_CELL_CTRL_TEXT_CROP` (lv_table.c:837), the roller's selected text (lv_roller.c:583), the textarea one-line placeholder (lv_textarea.c:1405) and any user code that sets EXPAND all reach this branch with `w = 0`. It happens to be harmless today only because `lv_text_get_next_line` returns early for EXPAND. Any backend or future change that uses `w` for EXPAND text will break line layout for every non-label caller."

    "failure_scenario": "The struct layout/ABI changes, breaking prebuilt binaries and binding generators that assume the old field order. Users building a draw dsc by hand have no idea they may need to set `text_size`, and custom draw-task handlers that change `dsc->text` leave the size out of sync with the text."
